note: Read the complete RFC 7607 and every tagged unit for this row. Section 2 says: If a BGP speaker receives zero as the peer AS in an OPEN message, it MUST abort the connection and send a NOTIFICATION with Error Code "OPEN Message Error" and subcode "Bad Peer AS" (see Section 6 of [RFC4271]). The older TestHandleOpenRejectsPeerASZero covers My AS zero and AS_TRANS with a zero Four-octet AS capability, exact notification 2/2 and no OpenConfirm; matching configured real-AS controls reach OpenConfirm with no notification. TestProcessOpenRejectsPeerASZero supplies the pre-parsed collision consumer with My AS zero versus a real AS and checks the exact notification/error versus success. Those older tests alone do not observe TCP abort. The new TestRFC7607ZeroASOpenAbortsTCP supplies both field encodings on real loopback TCP through ordinary ReadAndProcess/handleOpen and pre-read acceptWithOpen/processOpen, requires the complete notification payload [2,2], then a zero-byte read with io.EOF and Idle. It starts no Session.Run, so outer teardown cannot conceal a missing producer close, and cleanup runs after these assertions. TestRFC7607RealASOpenRetainsTCP pairs each case with a matching real AS, reaches Established through the actual OPEN/KEEPALIVE exchange and sends a further KEEPALIVE on the same TCP connection. The parent baseline log names all eight cases passing. Existing native records remove the notification while preserving close and force valid AS rejection; the queued new records must additionally observe closure omission and valid-AS refusal before stamping. The collision test exercises the winner consumer and handoff, not the separate identifier election. This supersedes the unstamped weak proposal based only on the older units and makes no judgment about RFC7607-2-1, -2-2 or -2-3.
